title: SNMP Manager Driver Configuration
description: Per-driver-type schema for `type: snmp_client` entries (FR-SB-006; Sprint C8, XEDGE-481/487; CRD §4.6). SNMP manager role via `pysnmp` (ADR-012 §2) -- GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK against field devices, plus SET write-back. One driver instance polls one device, matching every other driver type's convention. The agent role (xEdge itself pollable), TRAP/INFORM origination and reception, and MIB upload/parse are separate features -- see xedge/northbound/snmp_agent.py, xedge/core/snmp_notify.py, and the snmp_trap_receiver driver type respectively.

version.description: SNMP message processing model. v3 is the only version with USM authentication/privacy -- v1/v2c security is the community string alone, sent in cleartext on the wire.

community.description: Required for version v1/v2c. Sent in cleartext (no confidentiality in v1/v2c by design) -- prefer v3 for anything beyond a trusted management LAN.

v3_auth_protocol.description: USM authentication protocol. 'none' means noAuthNoPriv regardless of v3_priv_protocol.

v3_priv_protocol.description: USM privacy (encryption) protocol. Requires v3_auth_protocol != 'none' (authPriv needs authNoPriv first, per RFC 3414) -- privacy without authentication is not a valid USM security level.

consecutive_failure_threshold.description: Consecutive request timeouts (errorIndication) before this instance's connectivity_state moves to Not Connected -- same semantics as xedge.drivers.modbus.polling's identical field. SNMP is connectionless (UDP): there is no session to tear down and reconnect, so this tracker, not a connect()/disconnect() cycle, is what represents device reachability.

recovery_threshold.description: Consecutive successful requests required to leave Not Connected and report Connected again. See xedge.drivers.modbus.polling's identical field for the rationale (deliberately independent of consecutive_failure_threshold).

scan_rate_ms.description: FR-SA-009: 50ms minimum, 24h maximum -- this floor has not been lowered the way Modbus's was (XEDGE-413); it is a schema limit, not a verified achievable rate for UDP request/response over an arbitrary network path.

deadband.description: FR-DP-006: applies to every numeric tag in this group.

use_bulk.description: XEDGE-481 GETBULK. Applies only to this group's operation: get_next tags -- GETBULK means 'the next N values after each OID', not 'the value at each OID', so it is never applied to plain get tags (that would silently return the wrong data, not an equivalent faster request). A get_next tag is read via one bulk_cmd(maxRepetitions=1) instead of one next_cmd when true; both are one round trip either way for a single-step walk. Not valid with version: v1 (GETBULK does not exist in the v1 PDU set) -- rejected at connect() time, not silently downgraded.

oid.description: Numeric dotted OID, e.g. '1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0' (sysUpTime.0). Symbolic MIB names (e.g. 'SNMPv2-MIB::sysDescr.0') are not accepted here -- see XEDGE-485 for uploading a MIB to resolve names in the Web UI's MIB browser; polling itself always uses the numeric form so a driver never depends on a MIB file being present at runtime.

operation.description: XEDGE-481 GETNEXT: 'get_next' reads the OID lexicographically following the configured one -- for a table column whose exact row index isn't known ahead of time. Ignored (treated as 'get') when the tag group's use_bulk is true; GETBULK already is a repeated GETNEXT.

data_type.description: Required for a writable tag (access read_write/write_only): the ASN.1 type SET must send, which pysnmp cannot infer the way pycomm3 infers a CIP tag's type from the controller's own symbol table. Ignored for reads -- a GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK response is already self-typed by the device.

scaling.description: FR-DP-003: engineering_value = raw * scale + offset. Ignored for a non-numeric tag value (e.g. octet_string).

access.description: Matches xedge.drivers.modbus.polling's identical field: 'read_only' rejects a write-back attempt; 'write_only' excludes the tag from this group's scan_rate_ms poll.
